macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Asian stocks slip as Nvidia earnings and Fed policy take center stage
items.summary: Asian shares fell, with Japan’s Nikkei down 0.6% and South Korea’s benchmark off 0.2%, while U.S. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures rose 0.3% and 0.5%, respectively. Investors are awaiting Nvidia’s earnings and assessing whether the artificial-intelligence rally can continue amid shifting Federal Reserve rate expectations.

items.title: Nvidia earnings emerge as key test for AI trade
items.summary: Markets are focused on Nvidia’s upcoming results, with analysts expecting roughly 90% year-over-year earnings growth on revenue of about $109 billion. Investors will also watch whether the company maintains its outlook under new management and how the results affect broader technology valuations.

items.title: Persistent inflation keeps Fed rate hike expectations elevated
items.summary: Recent U.S. data showed wholesale inflation rising at its fastest annual pace since 2022, while Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said price pressures remain too high. Markets are monitoring upcoming Federal Reserve communications for guidance on the timing and scale of further tightening.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise as earnings offset economic slowdown concerns
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq advanced as stronger corporate earnings helped offset concerns about slowing economic activity. Unchanged consumer spending and persistent underlying inflation have reinforced expectations that the Fed could raise rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting.

items.title: GameStop falls after revenue miss; GE Vernova jumps on dividend increase
items.summary: GameStop shares dropped about 5% after the company missed revenue estimates. GE Vernova rose nearly 13% after doubling its dividend, while investors continued to track corporate results and capital-return announcements for signals about market breadth.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $65,000 as whale deposits exchanges
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $65,000, while a large holder transferred 347 BTC—worth about $22.4 million—to Binance, Bitget and BIT, potentially adding selling pressure.[1]

items.title: Bitcoin wallet moves 4,582 BTC after six years
items.summary: A wallet dormant since March 2020 transferred its entire 4,582 BTC balance, valued at approximately $378 million, according to Lookonchain data.[2]

items.title: Bitcoin mining machines briefly redirected to OCEAN pool
items.summary: About 64,000 mining machines, representing roughly 13 EH/s of computing power, were temporarily redirected to the OCEAN mining pool. The episode did not compromise Bitcoin’s protocol or consensus rules.[3]

items.title: Cardano holders reject $5 million treasury copper proposal
items.summary: Cardano governance participants voted down a proposal to withdraw 22 million ADA—approximately $5 million—from the blockchain treasury to invest in physical copper.[1]

items.title: Project Faro attracts $270 million from 21 banks
items.summary: A consortium of 21 banks, reportedly including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank, committed about $270 million to Project Faro, a planned dollar-pegged stablecoin project targeted for launch in 2027.[3]

items.title: South Korean exchange Coinone reports customer-data access
items.summary: Coinone said an outsourced customer-service provider suffered unauthorized access, exposing phone numbers and customer-support conversations. The incident was reported to South Korea’s Internet and Security Agency.[3]

items.title: Russia proposes capital requirements for crypto depositories
items.summary: The Bank of Russia published draft rules that would require crypto depositories to maintain up to $2.8 million in liquid capital ahead of a planned digital-assets framework.[9]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: G-STAR 2026 and GTA 6 set to headline gaming week
items.summary: South Korea’s G-STAR 2026 is scheduled for November 19–22, with Grand Theft Auto 6 also set to launch on November 19. Other highlighted releases include Legion Front, Burning Sword: Death Sun, and Witch The Showdown.

items.title: BATTLE BEARS GOLD returns with crossplay
items.summary: SkyVu is reviving the cult-classic shooter BATTLE BEARS GOLD on Steam and mobile, adding crossplay and new content developed by longtime fans of the series.

items.title: Vindictus: Defying Fate confirms PS5 release
items.summary: Nexon confirmed a 2027 PlayStation 5 release for Vindictus: Defying Fate and introduced the original character Noctia alongside a new cinematic teaser.

items.title: NCSOFT schedules Cinder City closed alpha
items.summary: NCSOFT’s Seoul-set open-world shooter Cinder City will hold a PC closed alpha from December 4–6, with participation limited to adults and covered by a nondisclosure agreement.

items.title: PlayStation launches Black Friday promotion
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment Korea announced a Black Friday promotion, while its GTA 6 launch campaign was among the gaming stories receiving attention in the latest industry news rankings.

items.title: Halo adds Firefight to Campaign Evolved
items.summary: Halo Studios plans to add the classic four-player Firefight player-versus-environment mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved through a free winter update, with more details expected at Halo Fest in December.
